2607.05282.title: Wavelet Scattering Transform for Interpretable Schizophrenia Biomarker Discovery and Classification from Resting-State EEG
2607.05282.paper_summary: Schizophrenia is a debilitating neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by profound cortical network dysregulation, for which objective, clinically translatable EEG based biomarkers remain underdeveloped. Existing automated classification pipelines rely predominantly on static power spectral density features inherently blind to amplitude modulation dynamics and cross-frequency coupling, phenomena central to schizophrenia pathophysiology, while adopting epoch level cross validation strategies that introduce temporal data leakage, artificially inflate reported performance. This study introduces a mathematically principled diagnostic framework integrating the multi-order Wavelet Scattering Transform(WST), strict Leave One Subject Out (LOSO) cross-validation, and SHAP explainability for simultaneous EEG classification and biomarker discovery. Hierarchical WST coefficients capturing multi-scale amplitude modulation structure were extracted from resting state multichannel EEG. Subject-level ANOVA with Benjamini Hochberg false discovery rate correction identified significant biomarkers, with Random Forest and SVM classifiers evaluated under strict LOSO cross validation and subject-level majority voting. Second-order scattering coefficients encoding cross frequency coupling dominated the discriminative biomarker set, with gamma-band features most prevalent, demonstrating that temporal amplitude modulation constitutes the primary electrophysiological signature of schizophrenia. Electrode P3 was identified as the single most discriminative site. Under rigorous subject independent evaluation, the Random Forest achieved 90.48% accuracy (AUC = 0.9339; sensitivity = 95.56%). The proposed WST framework establishes a rigorous, interpretable standard for EEG-driven psychiatric biomarker discovery that can also be applicable in the detection of schizophrenia subtypes in the future.
2607.05282.paper_summary_zh: 精神分裂症是一種削弱功能的神經精神疾病，其特徵是深刻的皮層網絡失調，對於此病的客觀、臨床可轉化的基於腦電圖的生物標記仍然發展不足。現有的自動分類管道主要依賴靜態功率譜密度特徵，這些特徵本質上對幅度調製動態和跨頻耦合現象盲目，而這些現象對精神分裂症的病理生理學至關重要，同時採用的時期級別交叉驗證策略引入了時間數據洩漏，人工提高了報告的性能。本研究介紹了一個數學原則的診斷框架，整合了多階Wavelet Scattering Transform(WST)、嚴格的留一主體交叉驗證(LOSO)和SHAP可解釋性，以實現同時的腦電圖分類和生物標記發現。從靜息狀態的多通道腦電圖中提取了捕捉多尺度幅度調製結構的層次WST係數。經過Benjamini Hochberg假發現率校正的主體級ANOVA識別出了顯著的生物標記，隨機森林和支持向量機(SVM)分類器在嚴格的LOSO交叉驗證和主體級多數投票下進行評估。編碼跨頻耦合的二階散射係數主導了區分性生物標記集，其中伽馬頻帶特徵最為普遍，顯示出時間幅度調製構成了精神分裂症的主要電生理特徵。電極P3被確定為最具區分性的單一位置。在嚴格的主體獨立評估下，隨機森林達到了90.48%的準確率(AUC = 0.9339; 敏感性 = 95.56%)。所提出的WST框架建立了一個嚴謹、可解釋的標準，用於基於腦電圖的精神病生物標記發現，未來也可應用於精神分裂症亞型的檢測。
